prompt: When Scott mentions the engines at Stone Point, Liz advises him to

options.text: focus on the human aspect instead.
check the accuracy of specific dates.

evidence: Liz says technical details would make listeners switch off and recommends focusing instead on the impact Stone Point had on people's lives.
why: Her advice is to move away from mechanical detail and concentrate on the human impact, which directly matches option A.
trap: B: She does not ask Scott to verify dates. C: Rather than explaining more technical language, she advises avoiding that level of technical detail.
explanation: Liz wants the presentation to stay accessible and human-centred instead of becoming too technical.

prompt: The school is looking for new team coaches and managers because

options.text: the overall interest in sport has grown.
certain parents have given up these roles.
new types of sport are being introduced.

evidence: The speaker says they had excellent people last year, but some of those parents now have other commitments, so replacements are needed.
why: The vacancies exist because some previous parent volunteers can no longer continue in those roles.
trap: A: The speaker does not say increased overall interest is the reason. C: No new sports are being introduced as the cause of the vacancies.
explanation: The school needs replacements for parent coaches and managers who now have other commitments.

prompt: What does the speaker say is the most important thing a coach needs?

options.text: confidence about the rules of a particular sport
the ability to make children enthusiastic about a sport
commitment to training the team for a full season

evidence: The speaker says knowledge of the game helps and can be developed through coaching courses, but what is really required is the right attitude: motivating children and making the game exciting.
why: The ability to motivate children and make the sport exciting is the quality the speaker identifies as essential.
trap: A: Detailed rules knowledge can be learned through courses, so it is not described as the most important requirement. C: Full-season commitment is not presented as the key quality.
explanation: A coach's attitude and ability to motivate children matter more than already knowing every rule.

prompt: For parents who would like to coach rugby, one requirement is that they

options.text: can commit to two coaching sessions per week.
have their own child in the team.

evidence: Volunteer rugby coaches are told to attend the upcoming day when children register for teams and organisers provide parents with more information.
why: Attendance at the registration day is explicitly required for people volunteering to coach rugby.
trap: B: The schedule mentioned is one Wednesday training session plus Saturday matches, not two weekly coaching sessions. C: The speaker does not say coaches must have their own child in the team.
explanation: Prospective rugby coaches need to attend the registration and information day on the rugby grounds.

prompt: The tutor points out to Lara that in different markets, a brand of chocolate

options.text: has different proportions of the ingredients.

evidence: The tutor points out that the proportions of ingredients such as caffeine and sugar can vary to suit tastes in different countries; Lara has already covered advertising differences separately.
why: The contrast being added is about ingredient proportions changing between markets, so option A is correct.
trap: B: Advertising differences had already been discussed by Lara and are not the tutor's new point here. C: The tutor does not identify price differences as the relevant distinction.
explanation: The same brand can adjust its recipe for different national markets.
